# Task Instruction

Execute the following steps to produce `/root/renewal_playbook_updated.hwpx`:

## 1. Inspect task resources
```bash
ls /root/
ls /root/renewal_playbook.hwpx 2>/dev/null
ls /root/renewal_update.json 2>/dev/null
ls /root/followups.csv 2>/dev/null
```
Find and read `renewal_update.json` and `followups.csv` (they may be in `/root/` or a task-specific directory). Also locate `renewal_playbook.hwpx`.

## 2. Understand the HWPX structure
A `.hwpx` file is a ZIP (OCF) package. Unzip the original to a temp directory and inspect its contents:
```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/hwpx_orig
cd /tmp/hwpx_orig
unzip -o /root/renewal_playbook.hwpx
find . -type f
```
Identify the content XML files (typically under `Contents/` — e.g., `Contents/section0.xml`). Read each XML file to understand the document structure and locate all editable text.

## 3. Read the update data
- Parse `renewal_update.json` to get the new values for: customer name, current owner, renewal window, pricing band, escalation contact, and pricing note.
- Parse `followups.csv` to get the follow-up items. Sort/order them by the `sequence` column.

## 4. Write a Python script to perform the update
Create a Python script that:

### 4a. Extract the HWPX
- Unzips `renewal_playbook.hwpx` to a working directory.
- Records the original ZIP entry order (important: `mimetype` must be first and stored uncompressed).

### 4b. Process each content XML (section XML files)
For each section XML file:
1. Parse with `xml.etree.ElementTree`, preserving namespaces.
2. For each paragraph (`<hp:p>`):
   - Concatenate all `<hp:t>` text nodes to get the full paragraph text.
   - Check if the paragraph text contains any old values from the JSON (the JSON should have both old and new values, or you can infer old values from the original document text).
   - For field replacements (customer name, owner, renewal window, pricing band, escalation contact, pricing note): perform string replacement of old values with new values in the concatenated text.
   - For follow-up lines: identify the three existing follow-up lines (they likely follow a pattern or are in a recognizable section). Replace them with the CSV items ordered by `sequence`. Make sure to remove old follow-up lines entirely (not just append).
   - After modifying text, collapse all `<hp:t>` elements in that paragraph's runs into a single `<hp:t>` element containing the full updated text (to handle text fragmentation).
   - **Remove `<hp:linesegarray>` elements** from any modified paragraph to clear stale layout cache.
3. Verify the appendix sentence `이 부록 문단은 그대로 유지해야 합니다.` is preserved unchanged.
4. Write the modified XML back.

### 4c. Repack the HWPX
Repack into a ZIP file at `/root/renewal_playbook_updated.hwpx`:
- **First entry**: `mimetype` — stored with `ZIP_STORED` (no compression), no extra field.
- **All other entries**: use `ZIP_DEFLATED` compression.
- Preserve all original files (images, settings, etc.) that were not modified.

## 5. Validate
- Verify `/root/renewal_playbook_updated.hwpx` exists and is a valid ZIP.
- Unzip it to a temp directory and check:
  - `mimetype` is the first entry and is uncompressed.
  - The section XML files parse without errors.
  - The new values appear in the text.
  - The old values do NOT appear in the text.
  - The appendix sentence is preserved.
  - No `<hp:linesegarray>` elements remain in modified paragraphs.
  - The follow-up items appear in correct sequence order.

## Key technical notes (from prior successful runs)
- HWPX text is often fragmented across multiple `<hp:t>` tags within a single paragraph. Always concatenate before matching/replacing, then consolidate into a single `<hp:t>`.
- `<hp:linesegarray>` is a layout cache element. If left in a modified paragraph, it causes overlapping characters when the document is opened. Remove it from every paragraph whose text you change.
- The `mimetype` file MUST be the first ZIP entry and MUST be stored uncompressed (ZIP_STORED) for OCF validity.
- When using ElementTree, register all namespaces at the start (parse a file first to discover them) to avoid `ns0:` prefix pollution in output.
- Be careful with namespace handling: use `register_namespace` for all namespaces found in the document before writing.

## 6. Run the verifier if available
```bash
ls /root/test_output.py 2>/dev/null && cd /root && python -m pytest test_output.py -v
```

Web search results for query: "HWPX mimetype file content application/haansofthwpx"

Here are the most relevant web-search findings for **“HWPX mimetype file content application/haansofthwpx”**, focusing on what the **internal `mimetype` file inside an `.hwpx`** contains vs what some websites use as the **HTTP `Content-Type`**.

## Key findings (what the web results indicate)

### 1) Inside an `.hwpx`, the `mimetype` file is used as a signature
Hancom’s own technical write-up explains that an **HWPX file is a ZIP-based container** and includes a top-level `mimetype` file that acts as signature/format identification. ([tech.hancom.com](https://tech.hancom.com/hwpxformat/))

### 2) The `mimetype` file content is commonly **`application/hwp+zip`** (not `application/haansofthwpx`)
A Hancom Developer Forum answer explicitly states that for **`.hwpx`**, you can confirm the format via the **top-level `mimetype` file**, and that the stored value is:

- **`application/hwp+zip`** ([forum.developer.hancom.com](https://forum.developer.hancom.com/t/hwp-hwpx-mime-type-whitelist/1641))

A 2026 thread in the `hwp-foss` Google Group also says that Hancom appears to be using **`application/hwp+zip`** and notes that you can see that by opening the file and checking the `mimetype` file. ([groups.google.com](https://groups.google.com/g/hwp-foss/c/8FtrFvVeChk))

### 3) `application/haansofthwpx` shows up “in the wild” as an HTTP download Content-Type on some sites
Some Korean public-sector sites show downloads labeled with the MIME type **`application/haansofthwpx`** (as the HTTP/content metadata for the download), for example on a Goyang city page listing an `.hwpx` download as `application/haansofthwpx`. ([goyang.go.kr](https://www.goyang.go.kr/www/publict/ntt/BD_selectPublictNtt.do?publictNttSn=286348&q_publictJobSn=))

This strongly suggests:

- **`application/haansofthwpx`** is being used by some web servers as a **Content-Type header / download classification**
- but it is **not the same thing as the internal `mimetype` file content** typically used inside the `.hwpx` ZIP container (which sources above indicate is often `application/hwp+zip`).

### 4) Other MIME types you may see associated with HWP/HWPX
An older `hwp-foss` thread about MIME types found in a Linux viewer packaging / shared-mime-info context lists multiple MIME types for `.hwp`, and for `.hwpx` it lists:

- **`application/vnd.hancom.hwpx`** ([groups.google.com](https://groups.google.com/g/hwp-foss/c/64d9HQj3GQA))

The same thread criticizes the “`application/haansoft...`” style as not ideal practice. ([groups.google.com](https://groups.google.com/g/hwp-foss/c/64d9HQj3GQA))

### 5) “Officially registered” vs “used in practice”
A Hancom Developer Forum discussion about setting HTTP `Content-Type` for `.hwpx` notes (paraphrased) that **HWPX does not have an officially registered MIME type**, and suggests using **`application/hwp+zip`** only if your client has a custom agreed behavior; otherwise **`application/octet-stream`** can be used since HWPX is ZIP-binary. ([forum.developer.hancom.com](https://forum.developer.hancom.com/t/hwpx-http-content-type-application-hwp-zip/1752))

## Practical takeaway (based on the above sources)

- If you are specifically asking what the **internal HWPX `mimetype` file contains**, the best-supported answer from the sources above is:  
  **`application/hwp+zip`** ([forum.developer.hancom.com](https://forum.developer.hancom.com/t/hwp-hwpx-mime-type-whitelist/1641))
- If you are asking why you see **`application/haansofthwpx`**, that appears to be a **server-side/HTTP-side label used by some sites** (not necessarily the internal HWPX signature string). ([goyang.go.kr](https://www.goyang.go.kr/www/publict/ntt/BD_selectPublictNtt.do?publictNttSn=286348&q_publictJobSn=))
- If you’re building a detector/whitelist, you may want to recognize multiple real-world values, including:
  - `application/hwp+zip` (commonly used inside the file) ([forum.developer.hancom.com](https://forum.developer.hancom.com/t/hwp-hwpx-mime-type-whitelist/1641))
  - `application/vnd.hancom.hwpx` (seen in shared-mime-info contexts) ([groups.google.com](https://groups.google.com/g/hwp-foss/c/64d9HQj3GQA))
  - `application/haansofthwpx` (seen as a download/content type on some sites) ([goyang.go.kr](https://www.goyang.go.kr/www/publict/ntt/BD_selectPublictNtt.do?publictNttSn=286348&q_publictJobSn=))
